title: Chris Justice (Engenious Design) — 'If your organization's metrics don't fight each other, they aren't that good'
summary: Justice leads the engineering firm Engenious Design. He read Incorruptible and fixed on the airline whose stated goals pulled against one another, taking it as a description of the job his own leaders face: do it all, instead of managing to a single bottom line. He also found the book longer than he would like, and told readers to pick it up anyway.
blockquote:
If your organization’s metrics don’t fight each other, they aren’t that good. Because that means they are too simple to accurately reflect reality. 

This is one takeaway as I read Eric Ries  book “Incorruptible”. He cites the example of an airline that had these goals:
Lowest cost
Highest employee satisfaction 
Highest customer satisfaction 
Highest profits
